reading.body:
CyrusOne's Florence, Kentucky campus publishes 5 MW of IT capacity, the largest disclosed figure in a state where five mapped sites declare 9.55 MW between them.

That 5 MW is a nameplate ceiling, not a measurement. The campus covers 143,000 square feet of technical space, and at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, the load supports roughly 125 racks. At 300 kW per accelerator pod it is roughly 17 pods. Either way the facility is sized for enterprise and colocation workloads, below the per-facility capacity of large cloud platforms and far from the single-site power budgets that frontier model training consumes.

The gap is in disclosure. Only three of the five mapped sites publish a capacity figure at all, so Kentucky's true computational footprint is unknown. The published certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II and Green Globes, describe compliance obligations rather than compute density, and say nothing about what hardware runs inside.

What remains unpublished is decisive. Applied power draw, utilization rate, power purchase terms and grid interconnection are all absent, so 5 MW cannot be read as actual demand on the Kentucky grid. The suitability score of 50 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion missing. Whether this site matters to AI depends on tenants and grid headroom that no published figure describes.
